newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU monetary committee to meet on single currency.
newsitem.headline: EU monetary committee to meet on single currency.

text.p: The European Union's monetary committee will meet on Friday to discuss the introduction of the single currency, EU sources said.
"We will be taking up some of the issues which need to be addressed under the Luxembourg (EU) presidency," said one official familiar with the committee's agenda.
Among the items under consideration will be economic policy coordination under a common currency, an issue which emerged from the EU's summit in Amsterdam in June.
Although market speculation over a revaluation of the Irish punt has intensified in recent days, officials said the Friday meeting was not designed to address recent currency developments.
"We try to avoid meeting on Friday but it was the only day convenient to all the members," said another official.
It was unclear whether the group, comprised of national treasury and central bank officials, would take up the sensitive matter of fixing conversion rates to the euro.
EU finance ministers will meet informally in Luxembourg in September to discuss how best to minimise market speculation ahead of the euro's introduction on January 1, 1999.
Luxembourg monetary officials, however, have sought to play down discussions on fixing exchange rates, saying that there is a difference between talks on the subject and an actual decision.
Most EU monetary officials say an announcement on conversion rates is likely to be made when the countries joining EMU are announced in the spring of next year.
